comparisons.peer_topic: Capital ratio table and transition periods
comparisons.peer_summary: The provided table presents capital ratios and related information in accordance with Basel 3 Standardized and Advanced approaches as measured at December 31, 2024 and 2023, with ratios calculated using a five-year transition period related to the adoption of the current expected credit losses accounting standard.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC disclose the use of a five-year transition period for CECL adoption impacts on risk-based capital ratios. MS specifies that this deferral impacts risk-based capital amounts, RWA, and supplementary leverage exposure, with impacts phased in at 75% by January 1, 2024, and fully phased-in by January 1, 2025. BAC similarly notes that its capital ratios for 2024 and 2023 were calculated using the regulatory capital rule allowing a five-year transition period related to CECL adoption.

sentences.text: Beginning on January 1, 2020, MSBNA and MSPBNA elected to defer the effect of the adoption of CECL on risk-based capital amounts and ratios, as well as RWA, adjusted average assets and supplementary leverage exposure calculations, over a five-year transition period.
The deferral impacts began to phase in at 25% per year from January 1, 2022 and were phased-in at 75% from January 1, 2024.
The deferral impacts were fully phased-in from January 1, 2025.

(1)As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, capital ratios are calculated using the regulatory capital rule that allows a five-year transition period related to the adoption of the current expected credit losses accounting standard on January 1, 2020.

comparisons.peer_summary: Citigroup's binding CET1 and Tier 1 Capital ratios were derived under the Basel III Standardized Approach, while its Total Capital ratio and Citibank's binding ratios were derived under the Basel III Advanced Approaches framework.
comparisons.comparison: While MS and C both utilize the Basel III Standardized Approach for certain capital ratios, they differ in application and scope. MS applies the Standardized Approach to MSBNA and MSPBNA for all risk-based capital ratios at year-end 2024. In contrast, Citi derives its binding CET1 and Tier 1 ratios under the Standardized Approach but derives its Total Capital ratio under the Advanced Approaches framework. Neither C nor MS discloses a CECL transition deferral in the provided text, but C's use of mixed approaches contrasts with MS's consistent use of the Standardized Approach for the reported entities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Assessment Method and CECL Adoption Impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Compliance is assessed against the lower of Standardized or Advanced ratios, and GS Bank USA is phasing in an estimated reduction to regulatory capital from CECL adoption at 25% per year through January 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS Bank USA disclose a five-year transition period for CECL adoption impacts, phasing in at 25% annually starting in January 2022. MS states that deferral impacts were phased in at 75% from January 1, 2024, and fully phased-in by January 1, 2025. GS confirms that it started phasing in the estimated reduction to regulatory capital at 25% per year through January 2025. Additionally, both entities utilize the Standardized Approach for their risk-based capital assessment, with GS explicitly assessing compliance against the lower of Standardized or Advanced ratios.

sentences.text: Beginning on January 1, 2020, MSBNA and MSPBNA elected to defer the effect of the adoption of CECL on risk-based capital amounts and ratios, as well as RWA, adjusted average assets and supplementary leverage exposure calculations, over a five-year transition period.
The deferral impacts began to phase in at 25% per year from January 1, 2022 and were phased-in at 75% from January 1, 2024.
The deferral impacts were fully phased-in from January 1, 2025.

• The lower of the Standardized or Advanced ratio is the ratio against which GS Bank USA's compliance with the capital requirements is assessed under the risk-based Capital Rules, and therefore, the Standardized ratios applied to GS Bank USA as of both December 2024 and December 2023.

• Beginning in January 2022, GS Bank USA started to phase in the estimated reduction to regulatory capital as a result of adopting the CECL model at 25% per year through January 2025. The total amount to be phased in includes the impact of adopting CECL as of January 1, 2020, as well as 25% of the increase in the allowance for credit losses from January 1, 2020 through December 31, 2021.
